title: Management of neonatal hypoglycaemia: a comparison of neonates with different risk-factors
summary:
At present, there is only one national guideline in Germany addressing the care of infants born to diabetic mothers, which provides recommendations for the screening and management of low blood glucose in newborns. There is no consensus regarding the appropriate management strategy for all other at-risk populations. There is currently insufficient evidence to determine whether these groups differ with respect to the required frequency of blood glucose monitoring or the incidence, duration, and severity of hypoglycemic episodes. Furthermore, it remains unclear whether they exhibit similar clinical manifestations.

To summarise, it remains uncertain whether the guideline for the management of infants born to diabetic mothers can also be applied to newborns with other risk factors for low blood sugar after birth.
The aim of this study is to identify similarities and differences among the various at-risk populations.

To achieve this, a documentation form will be completed retrospectively on a one-time basis for each newborn included in the study. The documentation form will collect information on birth characteristics, as well as risk factors and clinical signs of neonatal hypoglycemia. In addition, data on the infant's feeding regimen, therapeutic interventions and treatment approaches, and blood glucose measurements (including the timing of measurements and the lowest recorded blood glucose value) will be documented.

The collected data will be managed and analyzed using Microsoft Excel and IBM SPSS Statistics.

interventions.name: For newborns born to mothers with gestational diabetes or diabetes type 1 a documentation form will be completed on a one-time-basis and retrospectively.

For newborns with other risk factors, such as preeclampsia, pharmacological induction, lga, sga, perinatal stress or late preterms (GA <37+0), a documentation form will be completed on a one-time-basis and retrospectively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Birth at Uniklinik Köln between 01.01.2025 and 31.12.2025, gestational age ≥35 weeks; primary admission to the maternity ward, and the presence of at least one risk factor for neonatal hypoglycemia.
Risk factors include insulin-treated or diet-controlled gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), maternal type 1 diabetes mellitus, maternal preeclampsia, labor induction, late preterm birth (35–37 weeks of gestation), small for gestational age (SGA; <10th percentile), large for gestational age (LGA; >90th percentile), and perinatal stress (umbilical cord pH <7.1, Apgar score <5, pathological cardiotocography [CTG], secondary cesarean section, vacuum-assisted delivery, forceps delivery, or neonatal adaptation disorder).
Exclusion criteria:
Birth outside the Uniklinik Köln, gestational age ≤35 weeks, primary admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), or absence of any risk factors for neonatal hypoglycemia.
